newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon should claim $1 bln from Israel - deputy.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon should claim $1 bln from Israel - deputy.

text.p: Lebanon should demand at least $1 billion in compensation from Israel for damage it has inflicted on the country since 1978, a parliamentary deputy said on Wednesday.
The deputy, Assem Kanso, is a member of the national leadership of Syria's ruling Ba'ath party as well as a member of the Beirut parliament.

"Lebanon's rights to compensation begin from the first day that U.N. resolution 425 was approve, and $1 billion is a small figure for the damage Israel has caused since 1978," Kanso said during a debate on the government's policies.
U.N. Security Council resolution 425, passed in 1978, ordered Israel to withdraw its troops from Lebanon immediately and unconditionally following its first invasion of the country.
Israel ignored the order and has occupied part of Lebanon uninterruptedly since 1978.

Israel launched a full scale invasion in 1982 to drive the PLO from Beirut and still occupies a south Lebanon border strip and routinely bombs and shells Lebanese territory in a war with Moslem guerrillas.
Damage Israel caused during a 17-day blitz on Lebanon in April intended to crush the guerrillas has been estimated by the Beirut government at $500 million.
"I demand that this file is kept open in all international forums and that $1 billion is kept as a minimum figure with an open ceiling until the occupation ends," Kanso said.
He was the second deputy to demand compensation for damage inflicted by Israel during the three-day confidence debate.
On Tuesday, parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said Lebanon should seek compensation in U.S. courts for 13 villagers injured in south Lebanon last month by U.S.-made shells fired by Israeli troops.

He said Lebanon should build its case on the fact that a five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire agreement in south Lebanon -- comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel -- ruled that Israel was responsible for bombarding Safad al-Batikh village, injuring the 13 people.
